claim_verdicts.evidence: `git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Dockerfile` lines 5-17 match the lesson's block character for character. Line 25 `COPY --from=build /app .` is the later use of the `AS build` name the prose mentions; line 19 is the second FROM.

"There are runtime images for production and SDK images for building your code". Measured locally: mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 = 917MB; the built donhang-api:stage-1 (aspnet:10.0 base + app) = 241MB.

restore: "uses NuGet to look for these dependencies and download them if necessary". publish: "compiles the application, reads through its dependencies ... and publishes the resulting set of files to a directory"; "the hosting system may or may not have the .NET shared runtime installed". -c Release: "optimized for production deployment". --no-restore: "Doesn't execute an implicit restore". -o: "Specifies the path for the output directory." CPM: versions in Directory.Packages.props. Only gap: framework-dependent output does not contain the runtime.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `dotnet publish` — compiles the projects and gathers the app and the packages it uses into one output folder, ready to run where the .NET runtime is installed.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Stated as fact in §4, summary line 3 and q5, so it is a behavior claim, not opinion. Docs: deterministic compilation (default on) gives "identical binary output for identical inputs", and those inputs include "The precise version of the compiler used" and "The current directory path" (/src vs a laptop path). publish also "creates a framework-dependent executable for the current platform": the image's /app has a Linux `DonHang.Api` launcher, a Windows laptop gets `DonHang.Api.exe`.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Nothing about the result is special to Docker: with the same SDK version and the same source files, `dotnet publish` in the image builds the same app from the same commands you would run on your own machine, and the output runs outside a container too.

issues.quote: the only difference is that every machine gets exactly the same SDK, because the image says which one.
issues.text: Unlisted claim, and it does not hold. `sdk:10.0` is a moving tag: ".NET images are regularly updated whenever a new .NET patch is published" (refs/dotnet-docs/docs/core/docker/introduction.md). Today it gives SDK 10.0.401, and the host has 10.0.300. Machines that pulled the tag at different times get different SDKs. global.json only sets a minimum (latestFeature).
issues.fix: Replace with: "the difference is that the SDK comes from the image, not from whatever is installed on the machine, so every build that uses the same image uses the same SDK." Add the sentence to the claims ledger (kind behavior, version_key dotnet).

issues.quote: the image only makes sure every machine uses the same SDK.
issues.text: explanation.correct (en and vi) repeats the false claim from §4: the `10.0` tag does not pin one SDK across machines or over time. The key (a) is still right.
issues.fix: Change explanation.correct.en to: "The `Dockerfile` runs the same `dotnet` commands a developer would; the image only decides which SDK runs them." Update the vi text to match.

issues.quote: the lab would take minutes to restart after a one-line edit
issues.text: Unlisted claim, and the measurement contradicts it. A full uncached `RUN dotnet restore DonHang.Api/DonHang.Api.csproj` in the image took `DONE 10.0s` (Restored ... in 5.69 sec), and `dotnet publish` took 11-12s. Redoing the restore adds seconds, not minutes.
issues.fix: Replace with: "every one-line edit would wait for all of those downloads again before the lab could restart." Do not give a duration, or measure one and add it to claims as kind number.

issues.quote: and every deploy downloads all of it.
issues.text: Unlisted claim, and wrong. Pulling skips layers the machine already has: "Docker already has all the layers from the first image, so it doesn't need to pull them again" (refs/docker-docs/content/manuals/engine/storage/drivers/_index.md). docker_image_pull.yaml says the same: a pull "only pulls its metadata, but not its layers, because the layer is already present". After the first pull, the SDK layers are not downloaded again.
issues.fix: Replace with: "You notice this when an image built and run on the SDK is several times the size it needs to be, and every new machine has to download all of it." Add to claims (kind behavior, version_key docker).

issues.quote: Only a change to a project file or package version makes `dotnet restore` run again.
issues.text: Unlisted claim, and 'only' is too strong. The restore layer also runs again when `global.json` changes (it is copied in step 3), when a newer `sdk:10.0` base image is used, and when the cache is cleared or `--no-cache` is used (invalidation.md: every step after an invalidated one runs again). §4's "it depends only on the project files" and q4 explanation c ("only when a project file or package version changed") have the same problem.
issues.fix: Summary line 5: "A code-only change never makes `dotnet restore` run again; a change to a file copied before it, such as a project file, does." §4: "it depends only on the few files copied before it, which change rarely." q4 explanation c: "This would be needed only when one of the files copied before restore changed, and none did."

issues.quote: 1 — every `[build 1/11]` to `[build 11/11]` step is marked `CACHED` (in a terminal: `=> CACHED [build 7/11] RUN dotnet restore ...`
issues.text: In a real run of `docker compose build api` (Compose v2.33.1), step 1 prints `[api build  1/11] FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0` with `DONE 0.0s`. It is never marked CACHED. All labels also carry the service prefix and padding, for example `[api build  7/11]`, so the learner's output does not match the quoted text.
issues.fix: Use claim 5's suggested_text. Say steps 2 to 11 are CACHED and step 1 (FROM) is reused without a CACHED label. Quote the labels as `[api build  7/11]` or describe them as "the build 7/11 step". Update claim 5 to match.

issues.quote: gathers everything needed to run the app into one output folder
issues.text: For this framework-dependent publish, the output does not contain the .NET runtime. §4 itself says running needs the runtime, and dotnet-publish.md says the host "may or may not have the .NET shared runtime installed" depending on the deployment type.
issues.fix: Use claim 3's suggested_text: "gathers the app and the packages it uses into one output folder, ready to run where the .NET runtime is installed."

issues.quote: `global.json`, which names the SDK version,
issues.text: global.json at stage-1 has `"rollForward": "latestFeature"`. That makes 10.0.300 a minimum, not the version used: the image builds with SDK 10.0.401.
issues.fix: "`global.json`, which says which SDK versions the repository accepts," (claim 4 suggested_text).

issues.quote: With the same SDK version and the same source files, it is the same compiled app you would get on your own machine
issues.text: Claim 7 is filed as kind `opinion` with needs_verification false, but the lesson states it as fact in §4, summary line 3 and q5. It is only partly true: deterministic output also depends on the build directory path, and publish adds a launcher for the build platform (Linux `DonHang.Api` in the image, `DonHang.Api.exe` on Windows).
issues.fix: Use claim 7's suggested_text in §4 and summary line 3 ("...give the same app as on your own machine" is fine without "compiled" and without byte-identical wording). Change claim 7 to kind behavior, version_key dotnet.

issues.quote: Running the finished app needs much less: only the runtime, not the compiler and the build tools.
